C24 and C20 use the same machinery and much of the same language, but C03 is marginally closest in overall formulation.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"WHEREAS there exists a labor dispute between the American Telephone and Telegraph Company ... and certain of its employees represented by the American Union of Telephone Workers (CIO)","parent_excerpt":"WHEREAS there exists a labor dispute between the Carbide and Carbon Chemicals Corporation and certain of its employees represented by the Atomic Trades and Labor Council, AFL","explanation":"The opening recital follows the same concrete party-and-union drafting pattern, with the disputants substituted."},{"child_excerpt":"such dispute threatens to result in a strike or lock-out affecting a substantial part of the communications industry ... which strike or lock-out, if permitted to occur, will imperil the national health and safety","parent_excerpt":"such dispute threatens to result in a strike or lockout affecting a substantial part of an industry engaged in trade or commerce ... which strike or lock-out, if permitted to occur, will imperil the national safety","explanation":"The child closely reproduces the operative statutory finding and adapts the affected industry and commerce description."},{"child_excerpt":"The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title II of the said Act. The Board shall report to the President in accordance with the provisions of section 206 of the said Act on or before June 8, 1948.","parent_excerpt":"The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title II of the said Act. The Board shall report to the President in accordance with the provisions of section 206 of the said Act on or before March 19, 1948.","explanation":"This operative provision is nearly verbatim, with only the report deadline changed."},{"child_excerpt":"Upon the submission if its report, the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the said Act, until the Board is terminated by the President.","parent_excerpt":"Upon submission of its report, the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the said Act, until the Board is terminated by the President.","explanation":"The continuation-and-termination clause is substantively verbatim, confirming reuse of the same administrative machinery."}]}
